Council determine the opportunities for consultation with persons, organizations and authorities that are considered to be affected by the proposed amendment to the OCP, as described in the Report, to be appropriate to meet the requirement of Section 475 of the Local Government Act. 3. a Bylaw be introduced to rezone a portion of the subject site as shown as Block A on the attached Survey Plan (Appendix I), from "Acreage Residential Zone (RA)" to "Multiple Residential 30 Zone (RM-30)", and a Bylaw be introduced to rezone a portion of the subject site as shown as Block B on the attached Survey Plan from "Acreage Residential Zone (RA)" to "Comprehensive Development Zone (CD)", and a date be set for Public Hearing. 4. Council authorize staff to draft Development Permit No. 7920-0141-00 generally in accordance with the attached drawings (Appendix II). 5. Council approve Development Variance Permit No. 7920-0141-00, varying the following, to proceed to Public Notification: (a) to vary Section F.1. of the "Multiple Residential 30 Zone (RM-30)" to reduce the minimum (north) side yard setback on Lot 2 from 6.0-metres to: • 5.0-metres to the principal building face of Building 3; • 4.4-metres to the porch column, porch, and second storey balcony of Unit 12 in Building 3; and • 4.2-metres to the north edge of the outdoor amenity pergola (structure). (b) to vary Section F.1. of the "Multiple Residential 30 Zone (RM-30)" to reduce the minimum (east) rear yard setback on Lot 2 from 6.0-metres to: • 3.1-metres to the east edge of the outdoor amenity pergola (structure); • 3.8-metres to the principal building face of Building 1; and • 2.9-metres to the face of the electrical closet on the east façade of Building 1. (c) to vary Section H.4.(a) of the "Multiple Residential 30 Zone (RM-30)" to allow visitor parking space one within the required (north) side yard setback, and visitor parking space three within the required (east) side yard setback of Lot 2. (d) to vary Section J.1.(b) of the "Multiple Residential 30 Zone (RM-30)" to permit outdoor amenity space within the (east) side yard setback of Lot 2. (e) to vary Section B.6(b) in "General Provisions" of the Zoning By-law No. 12000 to reduce the minimum indoor amenity space required for Lot 2 before cash-in-lieu may be applied for a 16-unit townhouse development from 37 square metres to 0 square metres. (f) to vary Section B.26(b) in "General Provisions" of the Zoning By-law No. 12000 to permit stairs with more than three (3) risers to encroach into setbacks on Lot 2 for Buildings 1 and 2 (Units 1-11). 6. Council instruct staff to resolve the following issues prior to final adoption: (a) ensure that all engineering requirements and issues including restrictive covenants, dedications, and rights-of-way where necessary, are addressed to the satisfaction of the General Manager, Engineering; (b) submission of a road dedication plan to the satisfaction of the Approving Officer; (c) resolution of all urban design issues to the satisfaction of the Planning and Development Department; (d) submission of a finalized landscaping plan and landscaping cost estimate to the specifications and satisfaction of the Planning and Development Department; (e) submission of a finalized tree survey and a statement regarding tree preservation to the satisfaction of the City Landscape Architect; (f) the applicant satisfy the deficiency in tree replacement on the site, to the satisfaction of the Planning and Development Department; (g) the applicant provide a density bonus amenity contribution consistent with the Tier 2 Capital Projects CACs in support of the requested increased density, to the satisfaction of the General Manager, Planning and Development Department; (h) provision of cash-in-lieu contribution to satisfy the indoor amenity space requirement of the RM-30 Zone, at the rate in effect at the time of Final Adoption; (i) demolition of existing buildings and structures to the satisfaction of the Planning and Development Department; (j) registration of a volumetric right-of-way for public rights-of-passage over the publicly accessible open space (corner plazas) within the site; (k) registration of reciprocal access easements to ensure access to the proposed shared outdoor amenity facilities within the development; and (l) registration of a Section 219 Restrictive Covenant to adequately address the City’s needs with respect to public art, to the satisfaction of the General Manager, Parks, Recreation and Culture and with respect to the City’s Affordable Housing Strategy and Tier 1 Capital Project CACs, to the satisfaction of the General Manager, Planning & Development Services. 7. Council pass a resolution to amend the Stage 1 Anniedale-Tynehead Neighbourhood Concept Plan, approved under Corporate Report R167 (September 5, 2024), redesignating a portion of the site (Block A) from "Low Rise Residential - Type I" to "Townhouse", and another portion of the site (Block B) to "Low Rise Residential - Type II", when the project is considered for final adoption (Appendix VIII).

Title: Planning Report - Application No. 7912-0140-00
Motion text: That: 1. should Council grant First and Second Reading to the subject Comprehensive Development Zone, Council is requested to direct staff to file Bylaw No. 17764 previously brought forward for this project and granted Third Reading on October 1, 2012. 2. a Bylaw be introduced to rezone the properties at 2112 - 160 Street, 16197 - 20 Avenue, 16211 - 20 Avenue, 16219 - 20 Avenue, the portion of 16113 - 20 Avenue shown as Block 3, the portion of 16203 - 20 Avenue shown as Block 1, and the portion of 16273 - 20 Avenue shown as Block 2 on the attached Survey Plan (Appendix I), from "Acreage Residential Zone (RA)" to "Comprehensive Development Zone (CD)", and a date be set for Public Hearing. 3. Council authorize staff to draft the updated General Development Permit No. 7912-0140-00 generally in accordance with the attached drawings (Appendix I), and the finalized Ecosystem Development Plan. 4. Council instruct staff to resolve the following issues prior to final adoption: (a) ensure that all engineering requirements and issues including restrictive covenants, dedications, and rights-of-way where necessary, are addressed to the satisfaction of the General Manager, Engineering; (b) submission of a subdivision layout to the satisfaction of the Approving Officer; (c) approval from the Ministry of Transportation & Transit; (d) resolution of all urban design issues to the satisfaction of the Planning and Development Department; (e) submission of a finalized landscaping plan and landscaping cost estimate to the specifications and satisfaction of the Planning and Development Department; (f) submission of a finalized tree survey and a statement regarding tree preservation to the satisfaction of the City Landscape Architect; (g) the applicant satisfy the deficiency in tree replacement on the site, to the satisfaction of the Planning and Development Department; (h) demolition of existing buildings and structures to the satisfaction of the Planning and Development Department; (i) submission of a finalized Ecosystem Development Plan to the satisfaction of City staff; (j) the applicant satisfy the requirements for a P-15 agreement; (k) registration of a combined Statutory Right-of-Way / Section 219 Restrictive Covenant over the designated Streamside Protection Area for both "No Build" and conveyance access; (l) registration of a No-Build Section 219 Restrictive Covenant on proposed Lot 3 until vehicular access to Lot 3 is provided, to the satisfaction of the City; (m) registration of an access easement for proposed riparian Lot 4, to provide legal frontage; (n) registration of a Section 219 Restrictive Covenant to adequately address the City’s needs with respect to public art, to the satisfaction of the General Manager, Parks, Recreation and Culture; (o) registration of a blanket cross access easement to allow full-movement access to Croydon Drive in favour of the property to the north at 2172 - 160 Street; and (p) registration of a No-Build Section 219 Restrictive Covenant on Lot 1, to remain on title until Water Sustainability Act approvals are granted for the Carlson Creek tributary works. 5. Council pass a resolution to amend the Highway 99 Corridor Local Area Plan (LAP) to redesignate the land from Business Park/Light Industrial to Commercial, when the project is considered for final adoption.

Council determine the opportunities for consultation with persons, organizations and authorities that are considered to be affected by the proposed amendment to the OCP, as described in the Report, to be appropriate to meet the requirement of Section 475 of the Local Government Act. 3. a Bylaw be introduced to rezone 9366, 9400, and 9424 - 172 Street, and the portions of 9450 - 172 Street and 17246 - 96 Avenue as shown as Block 1 on the attached Survey Plan (Appendix I), from "Acreage Residential Zone (RA)" to "Multiple Residential 30 Zone (RM-30)", and a date be set for Public Hearing. 4. Council authorize staff to draft Development Permit No. 7921-0047-00 generally in accordance with the attached drawings (Appendix III), and the finalized Ecosystem Development Plan. 5. Council approve Development Variance Permit No. 7921-0047-00, varying the following Sections in the Zoning By-law, to proceed to Public Notification: (a) to vary Section F.1. of the "Multiple Residential 30 Zone (RM-30)" to reduce the minimum (west) side yard setback on Lot 1 from 6.0 metres to 2.0 metres; (b) to vary Section B.26(b) in "General Provisions" to permit stairs with more than three risers to encroach into setbacks on Lot 1 for Buildings 1-2, 7, 9, 13, 15, 20, 22, and 24; and (c) to vary Section B.1 in "Streamside Protection" to reduce the minimum setback distance for a Class B (yellow-coded) stream from 15.0 metres to 3.7 metres, measured from top-of-bank. 6. Council instruct staff to resolve the following issues prior to final adoption: (a) ensure that all engineering requirements and issues including restrictive covenants, dedications, and rights-of-way where necessary, are addressed to the satisfaction of the General Manager, Engineering; (b) submission of a subdivision layout to the satisfaction of the Approving Officer; (c) input from the Ministry of Transportation & Transit; (d) resolution of all urban design issues to the satisfaction of the Planning and Development Department; (e) submission of a finalized landscaping plan and landscaping cost estimate to the specifications and satisfaction of the Planning and Development Department; (f) submission of a finalized tree survey and a statement regarding tree preservation to the satisfaction of the City Landscape Architect; (g) the applicant satisfy the deficiency in tree replacement on the site, to the satisfaction of the Planning and Development Department; (h) submission of a finalized Ecosystem Development Plan and Impact Mitigation Plan to the satisfaction of City staff; (i) the applicant satisfy the requirements for a restoration agreement; (j) voluntary conveyance of the riparian area (Lot 2) to the City; (k) provision of cash-in-lieu contribution to satisfy the indoor amenity space requirement of the "Multiple Residential 30 Zone (RM-30)", at the rate in effect at the time of Final Adoption; (l) demolition of existing buildings and structures to the satisfaction of the Planning and Development Department; (m) registration of a volumetric right-of-way for public rights-of-passage over the publicly accessible open space (corner plazas) within the site; and (n) registration of a Section 219 Restrictive Covenant to adequately address the City’s needs with respect to public art, to the satisfaction of the General Manager, Parks, Recreation and Culture and with respect to the City’s Affordable Housing Strategy and Tier 1 Capital Project CACs, to the satisfaction of the General Manager, Planning & Development. 7. Council pass a resolution to amend the Stage 1 Anniedale-Tynehead NCP’s Transportation Concept (CR R167; 2024) to amend the road network by replacing the local road requirement with a pedestrian access, as shown in Appendix VIII, when the project is considered for Final Adoption.

Title: Planning Report - Application No. 7925-0208-00, 7925-0208-01
Motion text: That: 1. should Council grant First and Second Reading to the subject application’s Official Community Plan (OCP) and Rezoning Bylaws, Council is requested to file OCP Amendment Bylaw No. 21408, Rezoning Bylaw No. 21409 and Housing Agreement Bylaw No. 21410 and close Land Development Project No. 7920-0304-00. 2. an OCP amendment Bylaw be introduced to amend Figure 16: Downtown Densities from "3.5 FAR" to "5.5 FAR", and a date be set for Public Hearing. 3. Council determine the opportunities for consultation with persons, organizations and authorities that are considered to be affected by the proposed amendment to the OCP, as described in the Report, to be appropriate to meet the requirement of Section 475 of the Local Government Act. 4. a Bylaw be introduced to rezone the subject site from "Multiple Residential 45 Zone (RM-45)" to "Comprehensive Development Zone (CD)", and a date be set for Public Hearing. 5. a Bylaw be introduced to enter into a Housing Agreement and be given First, Second and Third Readings. 6. Council authorize staff to draft General Development Permit No. 7925-0208-00 generally in accordance with the attached drawings (Appendix I). 7. Council authorize staff to draft Detailed Development Permit No. 7925-0208-01 for Tower 3 (Phase 1) generally in accordance with the attached drawings (Appendix II). 8. Council instruct staff to resolve the following issues prior to final adoption: (a) ensure that all engineering requirements and issues including restrictive covenants, dedications, and rights-of-way where necessary, are addressed to the satisfaction of the General Manager, Engineering; (b) submission of a subdivision layout to the satisfaction of the Approving Officer; (c) resolution of all urban design issues to the satisfaction of the Planning and Development Department; (d) submission of a finalized landscaping plan and landscaping cost estimate to the specifications and satisfaction of the Planning and Development Department; (e) submission of a finalized tree survey and a statement regarding tree preservation to the satisfaction of the City Landscape Architect; (f) the applicant enter into a Housing Agreement with the City to secure 378 dwelling units in the proposed Tower 3 as rental housing for a minimum period of 60 years; (g) submission of a wind study report to the satisfaction of City staff; (h) the applicant provide a density bonus amenity contribution consistent with the Tier 2 Capital Projects CACs in support of the requested increased density, to the satisfaction of the General Manager, Planning and Development Department; (i) provision of cash-in-lieu contribution to satisfy the indoor amenity space requirement of the proposed Comprehensive Development Zone (based on the RM-135 Zone) for Tower 3, at the rate in effect at the time of Final Adoption; (j) demolition of existing buildings and structures to the satisfaction of the Planning and Development Department; (k) registration of a volumetric statutory right-of-way for public rights- of-passage for the area between the building face and the street edges, for the east-west walkway between Towers 1 and 2, for the north-south drive-aisle, and for the public plaza area west of Towers 1, 2 and 6; (l) registration of a Section 219 Restrictive Covenant to reflect the 378 rental units and ensure the proposal will adequately address the City’s needs with respect to Public Art, Affordable Housing and Capital Project CACs (Tier 1 and Tier 2) if the market rental tenure of the proposed development changes, at any point in the future; (m) submission of an acoustical report for the units adjacent to 104 Avenue and registration of a Section 219 Restrictive Covenant to ensure implementation of noise mitigation measures; (n) registration of a Section 219 Restrictive Covenant for "no build" for Lots A and B until Detailed Development Permit approvals have been granted by the City; (o) registration of a Section 219 Restrictive Covenant to adequately address the City’s needs with respect to public art, to the satisfaction of the General Manager, Parks, Recreation and Culture and with respect to the City’s Affordable Housing Strategy and Tier 1 Capital Project CACs, to the satisfaction of the General Manager, Planning & Development Services; and (p) final submission and approval of the Transportation Impact Assessment. 9. Council pass a resolution to amend the City Centre Plan to redesignate the land from "Mid to High Rise" to "High Rise Mixed Use Type I" and to delete the requirement for a public north-south road, as shown in Appendix VI, when the project is considered for final adoption.

Title: Planning Report - Application No. 7923-0238-00 – 17763 and 17773 - 24 Avenue
Motion text: That: 1. a Bylaw be introduced to amend Official Community Plan (OCP) Table 7a: Land Use Designation Exceptions within the Commercial designation by adding site specific permission for the subject site to permit a density up to 2.34 FAR (net calculation), and a date for Public Hearing be set. 2. Council determine the opportunities for consultation with persons, organizations and authorities that are considered to be affected by the proposed amendment to the OCP, as described in the Report, to the appropriate to meet the requirement of Section 475 of the Local Government Act. 3. a Bylaw be introduced to rezone the subject site from "Acreage Residential Zone (RA)" to "Comprehensive Development Zone (CD)", and a date be set for Public Hearing. 4. Council authorize staff to draft Development Permit No. 7923-0238-00 generally in accordance with the attached drawings. 5. Council instruct staff to resolve the following issues prior to final approval: (a) ensure that all engineering requirements and issues including restrictive covenants, dedications, and rights-of-way where necessary, are addressed to the satisfaction of the General Manager, Engineering; (b) submission of a subdivision layout to the satisfaction of the Approving Officer; (c) approval from the Ministry of Transportation & Transit; (d) resolution of all urban design issues to the satisfaction of the Planning and Development Department; (e) submission of a finalized landscaping plan and landscaping cost estimate to the specifications and satisfaction of the Planning and Development Department; (f) submission of a finalized tree survey and a statement regarding tree preservation to the satisfaction of the City Landscape Architect; (g) the applicant satisfy the deficiency in tree replacement on the site, to the satisfaction of the Planning and Development Department; (h) the applicant provide a density bonus amenity contribution consistent with the Tier 2 Capital Projects CACs in support of the requested increased density, to the satisfaction of the General Manager, Planning and Development Department; (i) demolition of existing buildings and structures to the satisfaction of the Planning and Development Department; (j) submission of an acoustical report for the units adjacent to 24 Avenue and registration of a Section 219 Restrictive Covenant to ensure implementation of noise mitigation measures; and (k) Registration of a Section 219 Restrictive Covenant to adequately address the City’s needs with respect to public art, to the satisfaction of the General Manager, Parks, Recreation and Culture and with respect to the City’s Affordable Housing Strategy and Tier 1 Capital Project CACs, to the satisfaction of the General Manager, Planning & Development Services. 6. Council pass a resolution to amend the Redwood Heights Neighbourhood Concept Plan (NCP) to allow a density of 2.34 FAR within the "Low Rise Mixed Use" designation for the subject site, when the project is considered for final adoption.

Title: Planning Report - Application No. 7918-0076-00 – 11275 - 124 Street
Motion text: That: 1. a Bylaw be introduced to amend the Official Community Plan (OCP) for the following: (a) Figure 3: General Land Use Designations for a portion of the subject site from "Urban" to "Industrial" (Appendix V); (b) Figure 42: Major Employment Areas by adding a portion of the subject site as an Industrial designation (Appendix V); and and a date be set for the Public Hearing. 2. Council determine the opportunities for consultation with persons, organizations and authorities that are considered to be affected by the proposed amendment to the OCP, as described in the Report, to be appropriate to meet the requirement of Section 475 of the Local Government Act. 3. a Bylaw be introduced to amend Official Community Plan Figure 51: Regional Growth Strategy Land Use Designations to amend a portion of the site from General Urban to Industrial (Appendix V), and a date be set for the Public Hearing, and authorize the City Clerk to bring forward the Bylaw for Final Adoption, subject to the Metro Vancouver Board approving Surrey’s amended Regional Context Statement and approving the Regional Growth Strategy amendments. 4. Council authorize staff to refer the application to Metro Vancouver for consideration of the following upon the application receiving Third Reading to amend the Metro Vancouver Regional Growth Strategy (RGS) designation of the site from General Urban to Industrial. 5. Council pass a resolution to authorize staff to submit a Regional Context Statement amendment application to Metro Vancouver following the application receiving Third Reading. 6. a Bylaw be introduced to rezone a portion of the subject site as shown as Block A on the attached Survey Plan (Appendix I), from "Urban Residential Zone (R3)" to "Light Impact Industrial Zone (IL)" and Block B on the attached Survey Plan from "Special Industry (I-4) Zone" to "Light Impact Industrial Zone (IL)" and a date be set for Public Hearing. 7. Council authorize staff to draft Development Permit No. 7918-0076-00 generally in accordance with the attached drawings (Appendix II), and the finalized Ecosystem Development Plan. 8. Council approve Development Variance Permit No. 7918-0076-00, varying the following, to proceed to Public Notification: (a) in Section B.1. of Part 7A "Streamside Protection", the by-law is varied to reduce the minimum setback distance for a Class A (red-coded) stream from 25.0-metres to 10-metres, measured from top-of-bank. 9. Council instruct staff to resolve the following issues prior to final adoption: (a) ensure that all engineering requirements and issues including restrictive covenants, dedications, and rights-of-way where necessary, are addressed to the satisfaction of the General Manager, Engineering; (b) submission of a road dedication plan to the satisfaction of the Approving Officer; (c) submission of a finalized landscaping plan and landscaping cost estimate to the specifications and satisfaction of the Planning and Development Department; (d) submission of a finalized tree survey and a statement regarding tree preservation to the satisfaction of the City Landscape Architect; (e) the applicant satisfy the deficiency in tree replacement on the site, to the satisfaction of the Planning and Development Department; (f) submission of a finalized Ecosystem Development Plan and Impact Mitigation Plan to the satisfaction of City staff; (g) registration of a Section 219 Restrictive Covenant Restriction against conducting repairs, maintenance and/or truck washing as well as refrigerator truck parking; (h) registration of a Section 219 Restrictive Covenant for payment of development cost charges (DCC’s) for the entire developed area identified and constructed as part of the permanent truck parking facility permit when a building permit is obtained on the lot; (i) the applicant address any unauthorized fill on the subject site and obtain fill permits as required. As a condition of obtaining a soil permit, a geotechnical report that addresses drainage and geotechnical concerns, both onsite and offsite may be required; and (j) the applicant address any concerns / requirements that the Ministry of Transportation and Transit (MOTT) may provide while seeking approval from the MOTT.

Title: Planning Report - Application No. 7925-0255-00
Motion text: That: 1. Council endorse the Public Notification to proceed for Bylaw No. 21807 to amend Comprehensive Development Bylaw No. 20151. 2. Council authorize staff to draft General Development Permit No. 7925-0255-00 generally in accordance with the attached drawings (Appendix I); and 3. Council instruct staff to resolve the following issues prior to final adoption: (a) ensure that all engineering requirements and issues including restrictive covenants, dedications, and rights-of-way where necessary, are addressed to the satisfaction of the General Manager, Engineering; (b) input and final approval from TransLink; (c) submission of a finalized Transportation Impact Assessment to the satisfaction of the Planning and Development Department; (d) resolution of all urban design issues to the satisfaction of the Planning and Development Department; (e) review of the project by the Advisory Design Panel and resolution of design comments to the satisfaction of the General Manager, Planning & Development Department; (f) submission of a finalized landscaping plan and landscaping cost estimate to the specifications and satisfaction of the Planning and Development Department; (g) submission of a finalized tree survey and a statement regarding tree preservation to the satisfaction of the City Landscape Architect; (h) submission of a Tree Cutting Permit signed by the neighbours for any off-site trees proposed for removal; (i) the applicant satisfy the deficiency in tree replacement on the site, to the satisfaction of the Planning and Development Department; (j) provision of cash-in-lieu contribution to satisfy the indoor amenity space requirement of the CD By-law No. 20151 Zone, at the rate in effect at the time of Final Adoption; (k) work with staff to explore mechanisms to encourage construction of the hotel component in the initial phase of the project; (l) registration of a right-of-way for public rights-of-passage for the proposed public plazas; (m) registration of a right-of-way for public rights-of-passage for the internal road, including sidewalks; (n) submission of an acoustical report for the units adjacent to Fraser Highway and 192 Street and registration of a Section 219 Restrictive Covenant to ensure implementation of noise mitigation measures; (o) discharge of the existing public art covenant; and (p) registration of a Section 219 Restrictive Covenant to adequately address the City’s needs with respect to public art, to the satisfaction of the General Manager, Parks, Recreation and Culture and with respect to the City’s Affordable Housing Strategy and Tier 1 Capital Project CACs, to the satisfaction of the General Manager, Planning & Development Services.

Title: Planning Report - Application No. 7922-0326-00 – 1891 and 1947 - 164 Street
Motion text: That: 1. a Bylaw be introduced to rezone a portion of the subject site as shown as Blocks 1 and 2 on the attached Survey Plan (Appendix I), from "Acreage Residential Zone (RA)" to "Comprehensive Development Zone (CD)", and a date be set for Public Hearing. 2. a Bylaw be introduced to amend Official Community Plan (OCP) Figure 3: General Land Use Designations for a portion of the subject site from "Multiple Residential" to "Mixed Employment", as shown in Appendix II, and a date for Public Hearing be set. 3. a Bylaw be introduced to amend OCP Figure 42: Major Employment Areas for a portion of the subject site by adding the area on the subject site, as "Mixed Employment", as shown in Appendix II, and a date for Public Hearing be set. 4. Council determine the opportunities for consultation with persons, organizations and authorities that are considered to be affected by the proposed amendment to the OCP, as described in the Report, to be appropriate to meet the requirement of Section 475 of the Local Government Act. 5. Council approve the applicant's request to vary the Sign By-law as described in Appendix IV. 6. Council authorize staff to draft Development Permit No. 7922-0326-00, including a comprehensive sign design package generally in accordance with the attached drawings (Appendix III), and the finalized Ecosystem Development Plan. 7. Council approve Development Variance Permit No. 7922-0326-00, varying the following, to proceed to Public Notification: (a) to reduce the minimum Part 7A Streamside Protection setback for an existing Class A watercourse (Carlson Creek) from 30.0 metres to a 14.4 metres at a pinchpoint; and (b) to reduce the minimum Part 7A Streamside Protection setback for an existing Class B ditch (Stream 1) from 7.0 metres to 2.0 metres at a pinchpoint. 8. Council instruct staff to resolve the following issues prior to final adoption: (a) ensure that all engineering requirements and issues including restrictive covenants, dedications, and rights-of-way where necessary, are addressed to the satisfaction of the General Manager, Engineering; (b) submission of a subdivision layout to the satisfaction of the Approving Officer; (c) approval from the Ministry of Transportation & Transit; (d) approval from the Ministry of Forests, Lands and Natural Resource Operations under the Water Sustainability Act; (e) submission of a finalized landscaping plan and landscaping cost estimate to the specifications and satisfaction of the Planning and Development Department; (f) submission of a finalized tree survey and a statement regarding tree preservation to the satisfaction of the City Landscape Architect; (g) the applicant satisfy the deficiency in tree replacement on the site, to the satisfaction of the Planning and Development Department; (h) submission of a finalized Ecosystem Development Plan and Impact Mitigation Plan to the satisfaction of City staff; (i) the applicant satisfy the requirements for a P-15 agreement; (j) conveyance of riparian areas and Biodiversity Conservation Strategy areas to the City, at no cost to the City; (k) registration of access easements, granting reciprocal access between proposed Lots 1 and 2 and between Lots 1 and 3; and (l) registration of a Section 219 Restrictive Covenant to adequately address the City’s needs with respect to public art to the satisfaction of the General Manager, Parks, Recreation and Culture. 9. Council pass a resolution to amend the Highway 99 Corridor Local Area Plan (LAP) to redesignate portions of the site from Business Park/Light Industrial and Buffers to Commercial and to modify the local road network, as shown in Appendix VII, when the project is considered for final adoption. 10. Council pass a resolution to amend the Sunnyside Heights Neighbourhood Concept Plan (NCP) to redesignate the northeast corner of the site from Multiple Residential 30-45 u.p.a to Commercial and to modify the local road network, as shown in Appendix VIII, when the project is considered for final adoption.

Title: Planning Report - Application No. 7925-0095-00 – 9699 and 9711 - 137 Street
Motion text: That: 1. Council file Official Community Plan (OCP) Amendment Bylaw No. 20110 and Rezoning Bylaw No. 20111 and close Development Application No. 7918-0180-00 and all applications associated with that project. 2. a Bylaw be introduced to amend OCP Table 7A: Land Use Designation Exemptions within the "Downtown" designation by adding site specific permission for the subject site to permit a density up to 18.9 FAR, and a date be set for Public Hearing. 3. Council determine the opportunities for consultation with persons, organizations and authorities that are considered to be affected by the proposed amendment to the OCP, as described in the Report, to be appropriate to meet the requirement of Section 475 of the Local Government Act. 4. a Bylaw be introduced to rezone the subject site from "Neighbourhood Commercial Zone (C-5)" and "Urban Residential Zone (R3)" to "Comprehensive Development Zone (CD)", and a date be set for Public Hearing. 5. Council support amending the City Centre Plan to allow for an FAR of 18.9 within the "Employment" designation and pass a resolution when the project is considered for final adoption. 6. a Bylaw be introduced to enter into a Housing Agreement and be given First, Second and Third Reading (Appendix A). 7. Council authorize staff to draft Development Permit No. 7925-0095-00 generally in accordance with the attached drawings (Appendix B) 8. Council instruct staff to resolve the following issues prior to final approval: (a) resolution of all engineering requirements to the satisfaction of the General Manager, Engineering (Appendix C); (b) submission of a subdivision layout to the satisfaction of the Approving Officer; (c) submission and acceptance of finalized architectural drawings, including resolution of all urban design issues, to the satisfaction of the Planning and Development Department; (d) submission and acceptance of finalized landscaping drawings, including resolution of all landscape design issues, and a landscaping cost estimate to the satisfaction of the Planning and Development Department; (e) submission and acceptance of a finalized arborist report, including satisfying the required tree replacement, to the satisfaction of the Planning and Development Department; (f) the applicant enter into a Housing Agreement with the City to provide 180 residential dwelling units as rental housing for a minimum 60-year duration; (g) demolition of existing buildings and structures to the satisfaction of the Planning and Development Department; (h) registration of a right-of-way for public rights-of-passage for the publicly accessible corner plaza at the northwest corner of the site; (i) registration of a Section 219 Restrictive Covenant to reflect the 180 residential rental units to adequately address the City’s needs with respect to Public Art, Affordable Housing and Capital Project CACs (Tier 1 and Tier 2) if the market rental tenure of the proposed development changes at any point in the future; (j) registration of a Section 219 Restrictive Covenant to adequately address the City’s needs with respect to public art, to the satisfaction of the General Manager, Parks, Recreation and Culture for the commercial portion of the proposal; (k) resolution of proposed tourist accommodation parking reduction to the satisfaction of the Engineering Department; and (l) registration of a Section 219 Restrictive Covenant to restrict the restaurant affiliated with the tourist accommodation to a limited-service kitchen operation that caters directly to the hotel visitors.

Motion text: That: 1. and (m) registration of a Section 219 Restrictive Covenant to adequately address the City’s needs with respect to public art, to the satisfaction of the General Manager, Parks, Recreation and Culture and with respect to the City’s Affordable Housing Strategy and Tier 1 Capital Project CACs, to the satisfaction of the General Manager, Planning & Development.

Title: Planning Report - Application No. 7924-0145-00 – 11426 and 11444 - 124 Street
Motion text: That: 1. Council approve Temporary Use Permit No. 7924-0145-00 to proceed to Public Notification and bring the Temporary Use Permit forward for an indication of support by Council. If supported, the Temporary Use Permit will be brought forward for issuance and execution by the Mayor and City Clerk once all outstanding conditions are satisfied. 2. Council instruct staff to resolve the following issues prior to final approval: (a) resolution of all engineering requirements to the satisfaction of the General Manager, Engineering (Appendix II of Initial Planning Report No. 7924-0145-00 dated November 4, 2024); (b) installation and subsequent inspection and approval of all required landscape screening and fencing works along the perimeter of the property, to the satisfaction of the General Manager, Planning & Development; (c) submission of financial securities to ensure that landscaping and fencing is maintained over the course of the Temporary Use Permit, to the satisfaction of the General Manager, Planning & Development; and (d) the applicant to undertake the necessary work and obtain permits, as required, for the proposed use of the existing residential building on the site for office space and washroom facility purposes or the applicant to undertake the necessary work and obtain permits, as required, for an on-site washroom facility. 3. Council is requested to direct staff to bring this application back to Council for consideration of file closure should the applicant not complete the conditions of approval associated with Temporary Use Permit (TUP) No. 7924-0145-00 within 180 days of Council providing support for the subject TUP.

Title: Planning Report - Application No. 7925-0315-00 – 13216 - 104 Avenue
Motion text: That: 1. a Bylaw be introduced to amend the Official Community Plan (OCP) Figure 3: General Land Use Designations for the subject site from "Multiple Residential" to "Downtown", and a date be set for Public Hearing (Appendix A). 2. a Bylaw be introduced to amend the OCP Figure 16: Downtown Densities to include the subject property within the 7.5 FAR category, and a date be set for Public Hearing (Appendix A). 3. Council determine the opportunities for consultation with persons, organizations and authorities that are considered to be affected by the proposed amendment to the OCP, as described in the Report, to be appropriate to meet the requirement of Section 475 of the Local Government Act. 4. Council support amending the City Centre Plan to redesignate the land from "Low Rise" to "High Rise", and consider passing a resolution when the project is considered for final adoption (Appendix B). 5. a Bylaw be introduced to rezone the subject site from "Combined Service Gasoline Station Zone (CG-2)" and "Urban Residential Zone (R3)" to "Comprehensive Development Zone (CD)", and a date be set for Public Hearing. 6. should Council grant First, Second, and Third Reading to the associated Rezoning Bylaw, then Council may wish to introduce a Bylaw to enter into a Housing Agreement, and consider granting First, Second, and Third Reading to Housing Agreement Authorization Bylaw No. 21855 (Appendix C). 7. Council authorize staff to draft Development Permit No. 7925-0315-00 generally in accordance with the attached drawings (Appendix D). 8. Council instruct staff to resolve the following issues prior to final approval: (a) resolution of all engineering requirements to the satisfaction of the General Manager, Engineering (Appendix E); (b) submission of a road dedication plan to the satisfaction of the Approving Officer; (c) final approval from BC Hydro; (d) review of the project by the Advisory Design Panel and resolution of design comments to the satisfaction of the General Manager, Planning and Development Department; (e) submission and acceptance of finalized landscaping drawings, including resolution of all landscape design issues, and a landscaping cost estimate to the satisfaction of the Planning and Development Department; (f) submission and acceptance of a finalized arborist report, including satisfying the required tree replacement, to the satisfaction of the Planning and Development Department; (g) the applicant enter into a Housing Agreement with the City to secure the proposed 230 residential units at varying rates of market and below-market rents, for a period of sixty (60) years; (h) provision of a cash-in-lieu contribution to satisfy the indoor amenity space requirement of the CD Zone, at the rate in effect at the time of final adoption; (i) submission of an acoustical report for the units adjacent to 104 Avenue and 132 Street and registration of a Section 219 Restrictive Covenant to ensure implementation of noise mitigation measures; (j) registration of a Section 219 Restrictive Covenant to adequately address the City’s needs with respect to public art, to the satisfaction of the General Manager, Parks, Recreation and Culture and with respect to the City’s Affordable Housing Strategy and Tier 1 Capital Project CACs, to the satisfaction of the General Manager, Planning & Development; (k) approval from the Ministry of Environment and Parks; and (l) registration of a statutory right-of-way for the proposed publicly accessible corner plaza.

and (k) registration of a Section 219 Restrictive Covenant requiring the applicant to pay all applicable contributions for Public Art, Affordable Housing and/or Capital Projects Community Amenity Contributions should the project be converted from rental housing to market units at any point in the future, after expiry of the Housing Agreement.

Title: Planning Report - Application No. 7922-0301-00 – 1755 and 1779 - 176 Street; 17558 - 18 Avenue
Motion text: That: 1. Council support amending the Darts Hill Neighbourhood Concept Plan (NCP) to redesignate the western portion of the subject site from Medium Density Townhouse to High Density Townhouse, to modify the land consolidation requirement, and to modify the local road pattern by deleting the north-south road and designating the road area to High Density Townhouse, and consider passing a resolution when the project is considered for final adoption (Appendix A). 2. Council endorse the Public Notification to proceed for Bylaw No. 21903 to rezone the subject site from Acreage Residential Zone (RA) to Multiple Residential 30 Zone (RM-30). If supported the Bylaw will be brought forward for consideration of First, Second and Third Reading. 3. Council authorize staff to draft Development Permit No. 7922-0301-00 generally in accordance with the attached drawings (Appendix B), and the finalized geotechnical report. 4. Council endorse Development Variance Permit No. 7922-0301-00, varying the following in the Zoning By-law to proceed to Public Notification and bring the Development Variance Permit forward for an indication of support by Council: (a) in Section F. "Yards and Setbacks" of Part 22 Multiple Residential 30 Zone (RM-30) to reduce the minimum south side yard setback from 6.0 metres to 4.0 metres for the principal building face and to allow patios and stairs within the setback area; (b) in Section F. "Yards and Setbacks" of Part 22 Multiple Residential 30 Zone (RM-30) to reduce the minimum west rear yard setback from 6.0 metres to 3.0 metres for the principal building face and to allow stairs within the setback area; and (c) in Section F. "Yards and Setbacks" of Part 22 Multiple Residential 30 Zone (RM-30), to allow patios and stairs within the north street side yard setback area. If supported, the Development Variance Permit will be brought forward for issuance and execution by the Mayor and City Clerk in conjunction with the final adoption of the associated rezoning bylaw once all outstanding conditions are satisfied. 5. Council instruct staff to resolve the following issues prior to final approval: (a) resolution of all engineering requirements, including satisfactorily addressing the Darts Hill Neighbourhood Concept Plan lot consolidation area requirements in terms of sharing required road construction costs, to the satisfaction of the General Manager, Engineering (Appendix D); (b) submission of a subdivision layout to the satisfaction of the Approving Officer; (c) approval from the Ministry of Transportation & Transit; (d) submission and acceptance of finalized landscaping drawings, including resolution of all landscape design issues, and a landscaping cost estimate to the satisfaction of the Planning and Development Department; (e) submission and acceptance of a finalized arborist report, including satisfying the required tree replacement, to the satisfaction of the Planning and Development Department; (f) the applicant provide a density bonus amenity contribution consistent with the Tier 2 Capital Projects CACs in support of the requested increased density to the satisfaction of the General Manager, Planning and Development Department; (g) provision of a cash-in-lieu contribution to satisfy the indoor amenity space requirement of the RM-30 Zone, at the rate in effect at the time of final adoption; (h) demolition of existing buildings and structures to the satisfaction of the Planning and Development Department; (i) submission of an acoustical report for the units adjacent to 176 Street and registration of a Section 219 Restrictive Covenant to ensure implementation of noise mitigation measures; (j) registration of a Section 219 Restrictive Covenant to adequately address the City’s needs with respect to public art, to the satisfaction of the General Manager, Parks, Recreation and Culture and with respect to the City’s Affordable Housing Strategy and Tier 1 Capital Project CACs, to the satisfaction of the General Manager, Planning & Development; (k) registration of a right-of-way for public rights-of-passage for the publicly accessible open space (corner plaza) in the northeast corner of the site; (l) submission and acceptance of a finalized Geotechnical Report and an associated Peer Review, to the satisfaction of City staff; and (m) registration of a Section 219 Restrictive Covenant that requires the owner to develop the site in accordance with the provisions identified in the finalized geotechnical report.

Title: Extortion and Criminal Activities in Surrey
Motion text: That: a. The City of Surrey recognizes that we are in a state of emergency due to the extortions and extortion-related violence which have plagued our city. The Surrey City Council formally urges the Government of Canada, given the national and trans-national nature of these crimes, to declare a federal state of emergency, or invoke equivalent extraordinary federal measures, to address the organized extortion crisis, including appointing an Extortion Commissioner for Violence Against Canadians to lead a profound federal response to extortions with their mandate to include overseeing: i. Immediate deployment of additional RCMP, federal organized crime units, and intelligence resources to Surrey; ii. Ensure Federal RCMP leadership of a joint federal–provincial–municipal task force with authority to act rapidly on extortion-related violence; iii. Fast-tracking removal proceedings for non-citizens charged or convicted of extortion, firearms offences, or participation in extortion criminal activity; iv. Expanding immediate detention and inadmissibility powers under the Immigration and Refugee Protection Act for individuals linked to organized extortion or violence; v. Leading changes to the Immigration and Refugee Protection Act to prevent refugee claims subsequent to extortion-related criminal investigations or charges; vi. Develop strategies to permit the public release of identifying information related to individuals charged and/or deported or wanted for extortion-related offences, in order to enhance public awareness and deterrence; vii. Foster close coordination between law enforcement and immigration authorities to prevent repeat offending; viii. Determine failure points in current legislative authorities that have given rise to this crisis and make urgent recommendations to improve performance of police on arresting, charging and prosecuting offenders; ix. Ensure cross-collaboration and meaningful execution of applicable transnational criminal intelligence information with provincial and municipal police resources; x. Ensure corresponding financial investigations of extortion-related crimes with diligent prosecution by all applicable agencies including tax avoidance and money laundering; and xi. Report to Canadians on a quarterly basis on the severity of extortion-related activities, and the progress in resolving this crisis; and b. Surrey City Council directs the Mayor to transmit these requests in writing to the Premier of British Columbia and the Prime Minister of Canada, copying the Ministers of Public Safety, Justice, Immigration, and Solicitor General, as well as local Members of Parliament and Members of the Legislative Assembly; c. Surrey City Council further directs the Mayor to send a formal letter to the Surrey Police Board requesting, within the confines of applicable law, the public release of identifying information related to individuals charged and/or deported for extortion-related offences, in order to enhance public awareness and deterrence; d. Surrey City Council affirms its solidarity with affected residents and communities, and commits to continued municipal advocacy until senior governments demonstrate measurable action to restore safety and public confidence; and e. City staff report back to Council within 30 days on responses received and any further actions required.

Motion text: That: 1. Council support amending the Redwood Heights NCP to redesignate a portion of the land from Park and Natural Areas to Townhouse Residential and consider passing a resolution when the project is considered for final adoption (Appendix A). 2. Council endorse the Public Notification to proceed for Bylaw No. 21924 to rezone a portion of the subject site shown as Block 2 on the attached Block Plan (Appendix B) from Intensive Agriculture Zone (A-2) to Multiple Residential 30 Zone (RM-30). If supported, the Bylaw will be brought forward for First, Second and Third Reading. 3. Council authorize staff to draft Development Permit No. 7923-0219-00 generally in accordance with the attached drawings (Appendix C), and the finalized Ecosystem Development Plan. 4. Council endorse Development Variance Permit No. 7923-0219-00, varying the following in the Zoning Bylaw to proceed to Public Notification and bring the Development Variance Permit forward for an indication of support by Council: (a) in Section F Yards and Setbacks of Part 22 Multiple Residential 30 Zone (RM-30), reduce the minimum side yard setback from 6.0 metres to 5.0 metres to the principal building face of Buildings 8 and 9, to 3.8 metres for Building 7 and to 3.0 metres for Building 11; (b) in Section F Yards and Setbacks of Part 22 Multiple Residential 30 Zone (RM-30), reduce the minimum rear yard setback from 6.0 metres to 4.0 metres to the principal building face of Building 16; (c) in Section B.26(b) of Part 4 General Provisions, permit more than three stair risers within the front, rear and side street setback areas; and (d) in Section B.1 Streamside Setback Areas of Part 7A Streamside Protection, reduce the minimum setback distance for a Class B stream from 15 metres to 10 metres from the top of bank. If supported, the Development Variance Permit will be brought forward for issuance and execution by the Mayor and City Clerk in conjunction with the final adoption of the associated rezoning bylaw once all outstanding conditions are satisfied. 5. Council instruct staff to resolve the following issues prior to final approval: (a) resolution of all engineering requirements to the satisfaction of the General Manager, Engineering (Appendix E); (b) submission of a subdivision layout and road dedication plan to the satisfaction of the Approving Officer; (g) voluntary conveyance to the City of the riparian area for conservation purposes, as well as the adjacent area for a public trail and drainage access; (h) the applicant enter into an agreement for Parkland acquisition for Block 1 on the attached Block Plan (Appendix B); (i) the applicant enter into a restoration agreement with the City; (j) provision of a cash-in-lieu contribution to satisfy the indoor amenity space requirement of the RM-30 Zone, at the rate in effect at the time of final adoption; (k) registration of a right-of-way for public rights-of-passage for the publicly accessible open space (corner plaza) within the site; (l) submission of an acoustical report for the units adjacent to 24 Avenue and registration of a Section 219 Restrictive Covenant to ensure implementation of noise mitigation measures; (m) registration of a Section 219 Restrictive Covenant to specifically identify the allowable tandem parking arrangement and to prohibit the conversion of the tandem parking spaces into livable space; and (n) registration of a Section 219 Restrictive Covenant to adequately address the City’s needs with respect to public art, to the satisfaction of the General Manager, Parks, Recreation and Culture and with respect to the City’s Affordable Housing Strategy and Tier 1 Capital Project CACs, to the satisfaction of the General Manager, Planning & Development.

Title: Planning Report - Application No. 7925-0099-00 – 2308 and 2388 - 128 Street; 12862 - 24 Avenue
Motion text: That: 1. a Bylaw be introduced to amend the Official Community Plan (OCP) Figure 5: Suburban Density Exception Areas to remove the subject site from the Suburban Density Exception Area (max 2 upa), and a date for Public Hearing be set (Appendix A). 2. a Bylaw be introduced to amend the OCP Figure 3: General Land Use Designations to redesignate the subject site from Suburban to Urban, and a date for Public Hearing be set (Appendix A). 3. Council determine the opportunities for consultation with persons, organizations and authorities that are considered to be affected by the proposed amendment to the OCP, as described in the Report, to be appropriate to meet the requirement of Section 475 of the Local Government Act. 4. a Bylaw be introduced to rezone the subject site from Acreage Residential Zone (RA) and Suburban Residential Zone (R1) to Multiple Residential 15 Zone (RM-15), and a date be set for Public Hearing. 5. Council authorize staff to draft Development Permit No. 7925-0099-00 generally in accordance with the attached drawings (Appendix B). 6. Council approve Development Variance Permit No. 7925-0099-00, varying the following in the Zoning Bylaw to proceed to Public Notification and bring the Development Variance Permit forward for an indication of support by Council. If supported, the Development Variance Permit will be brought forward for issuance in conjunction with the final adoption of the associated OCP and rezoning bylaws: (a) to reduce the minimum front yard (north) setback of the RM-15 Zone for Buildings 1, 11, and 12 from 7.5 metres to 5.0 metres; (b) to reduce the minimum side yard (west) setback of the RM-15 Zone for Buildings 7, 8, 9 and 10 from 7.5 metres to 5.0 metres; and (c) to increase the minimum south yard setback of the RM-15 Zone for Buildings 4, 5 and 6 from 7.5 metres to 10.0 metres. 7. Council instruct staff to resolve the following issues prior to final approval: (a) resolution of all engineering requirements to the satisfaction of the General Manager, Engineering (Appendix D); (b) submission and acceptance of finalized architectural drawings, including resolution of all urban design issues, to the satisfaction of the Planning and Development Department; (c) submission and acceptance of finalized landscaping drawings, including resolution of all landscape design issues, and a landscaping cost estimate to the satisfaction of the Planning and Development Department; (d) submission and acceptance of a finalized arborist report, including satisfying the required tree replacement, to the satisfaction of the Planning and Development Department; (e) the applicant provide a density bonus amenity contribution consistent with the Tier 2 Capital Projects CACs in support of the requested increased density, to the satisfaction of the General Manager, Planning and Development Department; (f) the applicant adequately address the City’s needs with respect to the City’s Affordable Housing Strategy, to the satisfaction of the General Manager, Planning & Development Services; (g) provision of a cash-in-lieu contribution to satisfy the indoor amenity space requirement of the RM-15 Zone, at the rate in effect at the time of final adoption; (h) demolition of existing buildings and structures to the satisfaction of the Planning and Development Department; (i) submission of an acoustical report for the units adjacent to 24 Avenue and 128 Street and registration of a Section 219 Restrictive Covenant to ensure implementation of noise mitigation measures; and (j) registration of a Section 219 Restrictive Covenant to adequately address the City’s needs with respect to public art, to the satisfaction of the General Manager, Parks, Recreation and Culture and with respect to the City’s Affordable Housing Strategy and Tier 1 Capital Project CACs, to the satisfaction of the General Manager, Planning & Development.

Title: Strengthening Municipal Controls on the Sale of Vapour Products in Surrey
Motion text: That Council direct staff to bring forward a report, with draft bylaw amendments for Council consideration, that builds on the 2019 framework and presents a "most restrictive legally supportable" option, including: a. A new business-licence class for "Vapour Product Retailer," requiring a specific licence to sell, offer for sale, provide, or distribute vapour products in Surrey, with enhanced compliance and inspection provisions; b. A major retail availability reduction measure, such as restricting vapour product sales to age-restricted 19+ premises only, and prohibiting vapour product sales in general-access retail settings, such as convenience stores and gas stations, subject to legal review; c. A cap and siting controls for vapour product retailers, including a citywide cap or caps by community, and minimum separation distances from youth- sensitive uses such as schools, parks, recreation centres, libraries, community centres, and from other vapour retailers; d. Companion zoning changes, if required, to align land use permissions with the licensing approach and enforce the siting rules; and e. An implementation plan that includes consultation with relevant health partners, enforcement and resource impacts, proposed fees sufficient to fund compliance, and clear consequences for violations, including suspension or non-renewal for repeat non-compliance.

Title: Planning Report - Application No. 7925-0150-00 – 4114 and 4148 - 184 Street
Motion text: That: 1. Staff will proceed with the application based on ALC’s decision and directives. 2. Title: Planning Report - Application No. 7925-0212-00 – 2563 and 2575 - 152 Street; 15158 and 15168 - 26 Avenue
Motion text: That: 1. should the subject application be granted First and Second Reading of the associated Official Community Plan (OCP) and Rezoning Bylaws, then Council is requested to direct staff to file: a. OCP Amendment Bylaw No. 20360; b. Zoning Bylaw Amendment No. 20361; and c. Development Permit No. 7918-0190-00; associated with Development Application No. 7918-0190-00 and close Development Application No. 7918-0190-00 and all applications associated with this project. 2. a Bylaw be introduced to amend the OCP Figure 3: General Land Use Designations for the subject site from Urban to Multiple Residential, and a date be set for Public Hearing (Appendix A). 3. a Bylaw be introduced to amend OCP Table 7A: Land Use Designations Exemptions within the "Multiple Residential" designation by adding site specific permission for the subject site to permit a density up to 2.8 FAR, and a date be set for Public Hearing (Appendix A). 4. Council determine the opportunities for consultation with persons, organizations and authorities that are considered to be affected by the proposed amendment to the OCP, as described in the Report, to be appropriate to meet the requirement of Section 475 of the Local Government Act. 5. a Bylaw be introduced to rezone the subject site from Acreage Residential Zone (RA) and Urban Residential Zone (R3) to Comprehensive Development Zone (CD), and a date be set for Public Hearing. 6. Council pass a resolution to amend the King George Corridor South Local Area Plan (LAP) to introduce a new land use designation: Low Rise Mixed Use Apartments (up to 3.0 FAR), when the project is considered for Final Adoption of the associated Rezoning and OCP Amendment Bylaws. 7. Council pass a resolution to amend the King George Corridor South Local Area Plan (LAP) to redesignate the land from Townhouses (25 upa) to Low Rise Mixed Use Apartments (up to 3.0 FAR), when the project is considered for Final Adoption of the associated Rezoning and OCP Amendment Bylaws (Appendix B). 8. Council authorize staff to draft Development Permit No. 7925-0212-00 generally in accordance with the attached drawings (Appendix C). 9. Council instruct staff to resolve the following issues prior to final approval: (a) resolution of all engineering requirements to the satisfaction of the General Manager, Engineering (Appendix D). (b) submission and acceptance of finalized architectural drawings, including resolution of all urban design issues, to the satisfaction of the Planning and Development Department; (c) submission and acceptance of finalized landscaping drawings, including resolution of all landscape design issues, and a landscaping cost estimate to the satisfaction of the Planning and Development Department; (d) submission and acceptance of a finalized arborist report, including satisfying the required tree replacement, to the satisfaction of the Planning and Development Department; (e) the applicant provide a density bonus amenity contribution consistent with the Tier 2 Capital Projects CACs in support of the requested increased density, to the satisfaction of the General Manager, Planning and Development Department; (f) demolition of existing buildings and structures to the satisfaction of the Planning and Development Department; (g) submission of an acoustical report for the units adjacent to 152 Street and registration of a Section 219 Restrictive Covenant to ensure implementation of noise mitigation measures; (h) registration of the Statutory Right-of-Way for a publicly accessible open space plaza at the corner of 26 Avenue and 152 Street; (i) submission to and review by the City of Surrey Advisory Design Panel; and (j) registration of a Section 219 Restrictive Covenant to adequately address the City’s needs with respect to public art, to the satisfaction of the General Manager, Parks, Recreation and Culture and with respect to the City’s Affordable Housing Strategy and Tier 1 Capital Project CACs, to the satisfaction of the General Manager, Planning & Development.

Title: Complaint Regarding Metro Vancouver and Request for a Public Inquiry
Motion text: WHEREAS the City of Surrey is a member municipality of the Metro Vancouver Regional District, the Greater Vancouver Water District (“GVWD”), and Greater Vancouver Sewerage and Drainage District (“GVSDD”) (collectively, “Metro”), AND WHEREAS beyond the reasonable expectations of the City, Metro has conducted its business in a manner that is unfairly oppressive to, prejudicial to, and disregards the interests of the City and other member municipalities, AND WHEREAS Metro’s officers and employees have withheld critical financial, engineering, environmental, and other records and information from the directors appointed to the Metro board by the City despite the directors’ fiduciary and statutory duties to the Metro’s board and the City’s ratepayers and residents, AND WHEREAS Metro entities have wasted corporate assets, AND WHEREAS Metro has violated the terms and conditions of provincial and federal enactments and of legal agreements, NOW THEREFORE the Council of the City of Surrey in open meeting assembled respectfully: 1. complains to the Inspector of Municipalities of the Province of British Columbia about the aforesaid matters of Metro business, 2. further complains to the Inspector about any and all bylaws, decisions, and actions of the Metro Vancouver Regional Board and the GVWD and GVSDD that have furthered the aforesaid matters, 3. requests the Inspector with approval of the Lieutenant Governor in Council to hold an inquiry that is open to the public, 4. requests Metro to pay all costs, fees, and expenses of the inquiry, and upon initial engagement by the Inspector, the City will deliver detailed and extensive particulars of the aforesaid matters of Metro business to the extent, if at all, required by the Lieutenant Governor in Council and Inspector to establish the scope and terms of reference for the Inquiry.

Motion text: That: 1. Title: Building Permit Compliance and Stop Work Orders
Motion text: That Council direct staff to review the City's current building permit, inspection, bylaw compliance, and stop work order process, and report back with recommendations to create a more customer-focused and compliance-based approach that: 1. Improves public education and communication around when building permits are required; 2. Makes the permit process easier for residents and property owners to understand and navigate; 3. Prioritizes voluntary compliance, education, and corrective action before enforcement, where there is no immediate life safety risk, 4. Ensures stop work orders are used immediately where work creates a serious life-safety concern, or where a property owner repeatedly refuses to comply with the City requirements; and 5. Provides Council with options for a more balanced enforcement framework that protects public safety while treating residents reasonably.

Title: Mayor's Health Advisory Panel
Motion text: That: 1. Council establish the Mayor's Health Advisory Panel as a volunteer advisory board to the Mayor and Council on community health and well-being; 2. The Panel include members with expertise in areas such as primary care, mental health and addictions, public health, seniors' care, child and maternal health, Indigenous health, health equity, patient advocacy, and health-systems policy; 3. The Panel provide non-binding advice on municipal actions, advocacy priorities, emerging health issues, and partnership opportunities; 4. Staff bring forward a draft Terms of Reference, including composition, appointment process, meeting structure, reporting process, and support through the City Manager's Office; and 5. The Mayor invite Fraser Health and the Ministry of Health to participate as non-voting liaison representatives.

Title: Expedited Tenant Improvement Building Permit Framework for Medical
Motion text: That Council: 1. Direct staff to report back to Council by the end of May 2026 with details on the new framework and the corresponding commitments on an accelerated timeline from permit application to permit issuance; and 3. Once the new framework is implemented, direct staff to report back to Council periodically to update Council on the success of the new framework and resultant delivery of new medical clinics and healthcare facilities across the city.

Title: Planning Report: Application No. 7925-0275-00 – 12841 Highway 10 (58 Avenue)
Motion text: That: 1. a Bylaw be introduced to amend the Official Community Plan (OCP) Figure 3: General Land Use Designations for the subject site from Urban to Multiple Residential, and a date be set for Public Hearing (Appendix A). 2. a Bylaw be introduced to amend OCP Table 7A: Land Use Designations Exceptions within the Multiple Residential designation by adding the following site specific permission for the subject site to permit a density up to 1.65 FAR, and a date be set for Public Hearing (Appendix A). 3. Council determine the opportunities for consultation with persons, organizations and authorities that are considered to be affected by the proposed amendment to the OCP, as described in the Report, to be appropriate to meet the requirement of Section 475 of the Local Government Act. 4. Council support amending the West Newton / Highway 10 Neighbourhood Concept Plan (NCP) to allow for mixed-use residential and commercial within the Proposed Local Commercial designation and consider passing a resolution when the project is considered for final adoption (Appendix B). 5. a Bylaw be introduced to rezone the subject site from Acreage Residential Zone (RA) to Comprehensive Development Zone (CD) and a date be set for Public Hearing. 6. should Council grant First and Second Reading to the associated OCP and Rezoning Bylaws, then a Bylaw to enter into a Housing Agreement will be introduced for First and Second Reading (Appendix C). Should Council grant Third Reading to the associated OCP and Rezoning Bylaws following a Public Hearing, it is in order for Council to consider the Housing Agreement Bylaw for Third Reading. 7. Council authorize staff to draft Development Permit No. 7925-0275-00 generally in accordance with the attached drawings (Appendix D) 8. Council instruct staff to resolve the following issues prior to final approval: (a) resolution of all engineering requirements to the satisfaction of the General Manager, Engineering (Appendix E); (b) approval from the Ministry of Transportation & Transit under File No. 2026-01985; (c) submission and acceptance of finalized architectural drawings, including resolution of all urban design issues, to the satisfaction of the Planning and Development Department; (d) submission and acceptance of finalized landscaping drawings, including resolution of all landscape design issues, and a landscaping cost estimate to the satisfaction of the Planning and Development Department; (e) submission and acceptance of a finalized arborist report, including satisfying the required tree replacement, to the satisfaction of the Planning and Development Department; (f) submission and acceptance of a finalized Ecosystem Development Plan and Impact Mitigation Plan to the satisfaction of the Planning and Development Department; (g) the applicant enter into a Housing Agreement with the City to secure the 69 rental dwelling units for a 20 year period; (h) submission of an acoustical report for the units adjacent to 128 Street and Highway 10 (58 Avenue) and registration of a Section 219 Restrictive Covenant to ensure implementation of noise mitigation measures. (i) registration of a Section 219 Restrictive Covenant requiring the applicant to pay all applicable contributions for Public Art, Affordable Housing and/or Capital Projects Community Amenity Contributions should the project be converted from rental housing to market strata units at any point in the future, after expiry of the Housing Agreement; (j) registration of the Statutory Right of Way for a publicly accessible open space plaza within the site; (k) discharge of Statutory Right of Way E2-23-0069; and (l) obtain Tree Cutting Permit(s) with written authorization from neighboring property owners for any off-site trees that are proposed for removal due to the proposed development.

(e) submission and acceptance of finalized architectural drawings, including resolution of all urban design issues, to the satisfaction of the Planning and Development Department; (f) submission and acceptance of finalized landscaping drawings, including resolution of all landscape design issues, and a landscaping cost estimate to the satisfaction of the Planning and Development Department; (g) submission and acceptance of a finalized arborist report, including satisfying the required tree replacement, to the satisfaction of the Planning and Development Department; (h) submission and acceptance of a finalized Ecosystem Development Plan and Impact Mitigation Plan to the satisfaction of the Planning and Development Department; (i) acquisition by the City of the Grandview Ridge Trail area; (j) submission and acceptance of a finalized Geotechnical Report to the satisfaction of City staff; (k) the applicant adequately address the City’s needs with respect to the City’s Affordable Housing Strategy, to the satisfaction of the General Manager, Planning & Development Department; (p) registration of a Section 219 Restrictive Covenant to specifically identify the allowable tandem parking arrangement and to prohibit the conversion of the tandem parking spaces into livable space; and (q) registration of a Section 219 Restrictive Covenant to adequately address the City’s needs with respect to public art, to the satisfaction of the General Manager, Parks, Recreation and Culture and with respect to the City’s Affordable Housing Strategy and Tier 1 Capital Project CACs, to the satisfaction of the General Manager, Planning & Development.

Title: Planning Report: Application No 7926-0041-00 – 14600 - 20 Avenue (the "Lands")
Motion text: That Council after taking into account the following criteria outlined in the Planning Report dated May 25, 2026: a) the impact of noise on the community if the application is approved; b) the location of the establishment; c) the person capacity and hours of liquor service of the establishment; d) the proximity of the establishment to other social or recreational facilities and public buildings; e) the number and market focus or clientele of liquor-primary license establishments within a reasonable distance of the proposed location; and after holding a Public Information Meeting in the form of a Public Hearing on June 15, 2026, in accordance with City policy, to gather views of area resident and business with respect to the proposed New Event-Driven Liquor Primary License at the Bayside Rugby Clubhouse; and after hearing any individuals who made a presentation to Council at the Public Hearing and after reviewing any correspondence submitted in response to the Public Hearing notice, Surrey City Council recommends support of the license subject to the following conditions: a) the applicant will enter into a Good Neighbour Agreement with the City; b) the hours of liquor service, when an event is booked, will be 11 am to 1 am Sunday to Thursday and 11 am to 2 am Friday and Saturday; c) the liquor service is event-driven only and liquor service hours of sale are limited to one hour prior to, during, and one hour after an event; and, d) the hours of operation for the associated outdoor patio area to be serviced will be 11 am to 10pm, seven days a week.
